name: DashTone – Custom Admin Styles
author: Planet 9

sections.description:
DashTone – Custom Admin Styles by Planet ⑨ adds an admin-only page under Appearance > Backend Styles.

Features:

  • Neutral grayscale color theme enabled on first activation.
  • Optional login-page and admin-bar logos using the WordPress Media Library.
  • Configurable backend, menu, submenu, accent, button, and admin-bar colors.
  • Optional left-navigation width and typography controls.
  • Optional “Built with ♥ by …” footer credentials.
  • Versioned JSON export and import, with logo images embedded and recreated in the destination Media Library.
  • Every feature can be disabled; empty logo fields preserve WordPress defaults.

The plugin does not contact external services and does not collect personal data.

Privacy

DashTone – Custom Admin Styles does not contact external services, add tracking, or collect personal data. All settings are stored in the WordPress database. Uploaded logos remain in the website’s Media Library.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin ZIP through Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin.
  2. Activate DashTone – Custom Admin Styles.
  3. Open Appearance > Backend Styles.
  4. Adjust the neutral defaults, upload logos, or import a JSON settings file.
sections.faq:
How do I restore the normal WordPress colors?

Turn off “Use custom colors” and save the settings.

Are logos copied into an export?

Yes. Selected PNG, JPEG, GIF, and WebP logo files are embedded in the JSON export. During import they are saved as new items in the destination website’s Media Library.

Who can change the settings?

Only users with the manage_options capability, normally administrators.
sections.changelog:
1.6.2

  • Renamed the plugin and directory slug to DashTone – Custom Admin Styles.
  • Updated the text domain, internal identifiers, option names, export marker, filenames, and documentation for the new identity.
  • Added automatic migration for existing settings and kept legacy JSON exports compatible with the renamed plugin.

1.6.1

  • Added a separate link color so accent colors can remain focused on controls, navigation, and focus states.
  • Added matching link colors to every predefined theme.

1.6.0

  • Prepared the plugin structure, slug, text domain, metadata, and packaging for WordPress.org.
  • Preserved compatibility with settings and JSON exports from pre-release Planet ⑨ builds.
  • Fixed import and reset redirects after moving Backend Styles to Appearance.
  • Hardened JSON upload validation and embedded-image dimension checks.
  • Improved compatibility scanning performance for dynamic admin interfaces.

1.5.1

  • Moved Backend Styles from Settings to Appearance.
  • Applied the accent color to native range sliders and detected parent focus rings.
  • Styled the Collapse Menu control and all toolbar hover descendants.
  • Removed automatic link underlines.

1.5.0

  • Replaced page-wide plugin exclusions with element-level WordPress style detection.
  • Applied custom colors only when controls use recognized WordPress default colors.
  • Preserved intentional third-party brand colors and styling.
  • Added support for dynamically rendered admin controls.

1.4.4

  • Preserved native content and button styling on all custom plugin and theme admin pages.
  • Kept the configured WordPress navigation and admin-bar styling active on those screens.
  • Added a filter so developers can override content styling for exceptional admin screens.

1.4.3

  • Applied the configured button colors and interaction states to page-title actions such as Add New Post.
  • Added support for the legacy WordPress Add New button variant.

1.4.2

  • Applied the configured link colors and hover states to WordPress link-style buttons, including Quick Edit.
  • Preserved the distinct destructive styling of delete actions.

1.4.1

  • Fully applied the accent color to selected and focused radio buttons.
  • Restored visible hover and focus feedback for links such as Quick Edit.
  • Standardized all user-facing copy on American English.

1.4.0

  • Added eight optional predefined color themes with compact previews.
  • Changed the default notification-counter color to a friendly blue distinct from the neutral accent.
  • Applied the accent color more consistently to links, checkboxes, radio buttons, and classic-editor controls.
  • Refined the settings-page introduction.

1.3.0

  • Applied the accent color consistently to links, controls, submenu hover states, and toolbar hover states.
  • Added a separate submenu text color and editable HEX fields.
  • Added a safe reset-to-defaults action.
  • Moved import and export to the top of the settings screen and renamed Credentials to Credits.
  • Set distinct default accent and notification-counter colors.

1.2.0

  • Refined the plugin identity and settings experience.
  • Fixed left-navigation sizing around WordPress responsive breakpoints.
  • Improved submenu accent states, notification badges, admin-bar logo replacement, and settings-page buttons.

1.1.0

  • Changed the settings screen to use standard WordPress styling.
  • Added notification-counter colors and left-navigation sizing.
  • Embedded logo files in JSON exports and recreated them during import.
  • Improved neutral defaults, credentials, status messages, and admin-bar logo handling.

1.0.0

  • Initial release.
